summaryJa: 文書は米国のUFO調査に関する公式態度と経緯を概説している。1947年6月にオハイオのATICが飛行円盤報告の調査を引き受け、当初はソ連起源を疑ったが一部調査官は惑星間起源の可能性を検討し、1948年9月にペンタゴンへ書面見積を出した。1949年2月にProject SIGMAの人員が入れ替わりProject GRUDGEが設置され、UFO受容を打ち消す動きがあったが失敗し報告数はむしろ増加した。1952年3月のProject BLUE BOOK設立後は約3,200件の報告をIBMカードで処理し、1952年夏に報告件数が20倍超に増加、ワシントンD.C.付近での目撃も含まれた。1953年1月のロバートソン・パネルは調査継続（人員・装備増強）を勧告したが、同年2月のCIA報告は公的には調査を打ち切る一方で情報収集を強化する方針を示し、同年9月以降BLUE BOOKは大幅に縮小され調査機能は4602nd AISSに移管された。BLUE BOOKは1969年閉鎖まで主に非機密の要約提供にとどまり、真剣な収集・分析の中心とはならなかった。1953年のJANAP 146や1960年改訂の146Eで軍関係者の発言統制が強化され、退役後に米政府がUFOの地球外起源を知っていると公言した関係者（文書は複数名を列挙）もあった。Project BLUE BOOK特別報告No.14では一部の本文が公表されず、統計解析は「科学的に未知の説明」を支持する結果も示したと記されている。また、目撃者信頼性と報告の分類に関する図表では、目撃信頼性が上がるにつれて「不明」比率が増え、「情報不足」比率が減る傾向が示されている。文書の冒頭でオーストラリア側の調査能力不足（情報・科学・広報の観点）を補うため、RAAFの提案に基づき他の政府部門に調査責任を移すべきだとする見解も述べられている。
summaryEn: The document summarizes official U.S. attitudes and the history of UFO investigations. In June 1947 ATIC (near Dayton, Ohio) assumed responsibility for flying-saucer reports; investigators initially considered a Soviet origin but some favored an interplanetary explanation and a written estimate was sent to the Pentagon in September 1948. In February 1949 Project GRUDGE replaced earlier personnel with an effort to discourage acceptance of UFOs; this failed and reports increased. Project BLUE BOOK was established in March 1952, processed about 3,200 reports into IBM-card-sortable form, and the summer of 1952 saw a more-than-twenty-fold rise in reporting including major July sightings near Washington D.C. A Robertson panel (chaired by H.P. Robertson) in mid-January 1953 recommended continued investigation with increased staff and equipment, but a CIA report of 16 February 1953 favored publicly abandoning the investigation while intensifying data collection. By September 1953 BLUE BOOK was greatly reduced and investigative functions were transferred to the 4602nd AISS reporting to Air Defense Command and USAF Intelligence. BLUE BOOK remained largely a source of unclassified summaries until its closure in December 1969 and was not the central body for serious collection or analysis. JANAP 146 (1953) and its 1960 revision JANAP 146E tightened restrictions on service personnel discussing UFOs (with severe penalties). The document notes retired or resigning intelligence officers (named in the text) publicly stated the U.S. government knew UFOs were extraterrestrial but withheld this from the public. Project BLUE BOOK Special Report No.14 contained unreleased sections; statistical analysis in the report reportedly favored an explanation that was scientifically unknown, though public summaries emphasized reducing residual unknowns. A diagram in the report showed that as observer and report reliability improved, the percentage classified as “unknown” increased while “insufficient information” decreased. The file also includes an Australian note that Australia lacked adequate intelligence, scientific and public-relations perspectives on UFOs and that the RAAF suggested another government department assume investigation responsibility.
